speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To understand the cause of your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, I need to ask some questions: When did these symptoms first begin, and have they been getting progressively worse? Are you experiencing any trouble with your swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with fluctuating double vision upon eye movement and limb weakness, is highly characteristic. I will not order further tests as the clinical presentation is sufficient for this initial diagnosis.
